page_title: Lunavect — Claude Code and Codex in your Mac menu bar

summary.name: Lunavect
summary.one_liner: A free, open-source macOS menu bar app that shows the live state of Claude Code and Codex sessions and their weekly and five-hour usage limits.
keywords: see which ai agent needs me
use_cases: Monitor several Claude Code or Codex sessions at once
Check weekly and five-hour usage limits without opening the tools
Get notified when an agent finishes or needs approval
Cap how much of the weekly allowance an agent session uses
Review working time and token usage per project or model
summary.what_it_does: Lunavect lists every Claude Code and Codex session on the Mac with its live state (working, thinking, waiting for permission or input, or done), with search, filter, pin and hide options. The menu bar shows weekly and five-hour usage limits for both tools with reset times, as bars, percentages or rings. Users can set a share of the weekly limit for a session so the agent wraps up its step and stops near that level, and can continue later. The app also offers desktop widgets, time tracking by day through year, and a token view built from local logs.
notable: Stops a session at a chosen share of the weekly limit without killing it
Desktop widgets that read saved data and work while the app is closed
Uses existing official sign-in; no API key needed
caveats: Claude requires the Claude Code CLI; Claude Desktop alone is not enough
Codex requires the official Codex app or CLI
Recovered history is marked approximate; activity is not the same as token usage
